mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and rising inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 12-month average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12mo avg for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is inconsistent and signals data inconsistency or sectoral shifts; under such conditions, S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days exhibit no predictable direction and should be treated as noise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns show statistically significant deviation (p < 0.05) from zero in the predicted direction in more than 30% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals increased consumer reliance on debt to sustain spending, which amplifies recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12mo moving average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
